latest_nl_proof:
Let N := r+a+b. Since 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, we have N >= b >= a >= 0; in particular 0 <= a <= N and 0 <= b <= N, and also N-a = r+b >= 0 and N-b = r+a >= 0. By the standard polynomial form of Gaussian q-binomial coefficients, for 0 <= t <= N one has [N choose t]_q = (q;q)_N / ((q;q)_t (q;q)_{N-t}). Therefore
[N choose b]_q / [N choose a]_q = ((q;q)_N / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{N-b})) / ((q;q)_N / ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{N-a})) = ((q;q)_a (q;q)_{N-a}) / ((q;q)_b (q;q)_{N-b}).
Using N-a = r+b and N-b = r+a, this becomes
[N choose b]_q / [N choose a]_q = ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b) = R_{a,b,r}(q).
Thus R_{a,b,r}(q) is exactly a quotient of two Gaussian q-binomial coefficients. By hypothesis R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q], so this quotient is a polynomial in q. Applying the allowed semantic anchor with n = N, k = b, and l = a, we conclude that every coefficient of R_{a,b,r}(q) is nonnegative. Since R_{a,b,r}(q) is in Z[q], all of its coefficients are integers. Therefore, for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer. This proves the lemma.

statement_nl: For integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, let q be an indeterminate, define (q;q)_n := product_{j=1}^n (1 - q^j) for n >= 0 with (q;q)_0 := 1, set R_{a,b,r}(q) := ((q;q)_{r+b} (q;q)_a) / ((q;q)_{r+a} (q;q)_b), and define D := r (b - a). Assume that R_{a,b,r}(q) belongs to Z[q]. Then for every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient of q^j in R_{a,b,r}(q) is a nonnegative integer.

domain_restrictions: a, b, and r are integers
q is a formal indeterminate, not a specialized numeric value
n ranges over nonnegative integers in the product definition
D is nonnegative because r >= 0 and b - a >= 0
j is an integer with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2)
R is assumed to be a polynomial with integer coefficients
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: Under the integer constraints 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0, if the quotient defining R is actually a polynomial with integer coefficients, then every coefficient of q to the power j in R is a nonnegative integer for all integers j from 0 through floor(r times (b - a) divided by 2).
quantifier_order: For all integers a, b, r with 0 <= a <= b and r >= 0
For each nonnegative integer n, define the q-factorial quantity
Define R from a, b, r, and q by the stated quotient
Define D as r times (b - a)
Assume the resulting R is an element of Z[q]
For every integer j with 0 <= j <= floor(D/2), the coefficient condition is asserted
